Solution B is correct and Solution A is not.

Solving the equation directly:

$|x-4| - 10 = 2 \implies |x-4| = 12 \implies x - 4 = 12 \text{ or } x - 4 = -12$

So $x = 16$ or $x = -8$, and the product is $16 \times (-8) = -128$.

Solution A makes an error when it sets up the cases. It says $x-4$ can be 2 or -12 because those numbers "have absolute values 12," but $|2| = 2$, not 12. The correct cases are $x-4 = 12$ and $x-4 = -12$. Its wrong cases lead to $x = 6$ and $x = -8$, and its product of -48 is wrong.

Solution B isolates the absolute value correctly, splits into the two cases correctly, and gets the right solutions. Its product of -128 is correct.

WINNER: B
